name: Engram
description: Engram is a modern disc ripping and media organization tool with a reactive web dashboard. Unlike headless automation tools, Engram provides full visibility into the ripping process with intelligent Human-in-the-Loop intervention for ambiguous content. SUPPORT: - Discord: https://discord.gg/G8fjjGswdc - GitHub Issues: https://github.com/jsakkos/engram/issues REQUIREMENTS: - A TMDB Read Access Token (set in the Engram web UI on first run) - Optical drive passthrough is REQUIRED. A native Linux host exposing /dev/sr* devices is needed. Use the Disc Drive (block) and Disc Drive (scsi) settings below; each variable's description shows the command to find the correct device paths. - A MakeMKV license key is OPTIONAL — the free monthly beta key from the MakeMKV forums is grabbed automatically if one is not provided. GPU ACCELERATION (OPTIONAL): - Enabled by default via --gpus=all in Extra Parameters. Requires the Unraid Nvidia Driver plugin, which bundles the NVIDIA Container Toolkit — no separate install needed. - If you don't have an NVIDIA GPU or don't want GPU acceleration, remove --gpus=all from Extra Parameters. FIRST START: - Slow: compiles MakeMKV (a few minutes) and downloads a speech model (~465MB) - Set PUID/PGID to your user IDs to avoid root-owned files (run 'id -u' and 'id -g' in a terminal)

paths.name: Config Path
paths.description: Database, caches, compiled MakeMKV, and settings.

paths.name: Staging Path
paths.description: Work area for in-progress rips and auto-import workflow (example path)

ports.name: Web UI Port
ports.description: Port to access the Engram web UI

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID — run 'id -u' in a terminal to find yours (99 = nobody)

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID — run 'id -g' in a terminal to find yours (100 = users)

variables.name: MakeMKV License Key
variables.description: Optional. MakeMKV license or free beta key from https://forum.makemkv.com/ (beta key updates monthly). Engram grabs the current beta key automatically if left blank.

variables.name: MakeMKV Version
variables.description: Pin a specific version (e.g., 1.18.1) for reproducibility, or leave 'latest' for the newest.

devices.name: Disc Drive (block)
devices.description: REQUIRED. Run 'lsscsi -g' and take the FIRST path for your disc drive (e.g., /dev/sr0)

devices.name: Disc Drive (scsi)
devices.description: REQUIRED. Run 'lsscsi -g' and take the SECOND path for your disc drive (e.g., /dev/sg3). Must match the same physical drive as the block device.
